title: Strain-enhanced superconductivity in RuO$_2$ thin films: Joint experimental and theoretical studies
authors: Moeen ud din, Tsun-Sung Kuo, Yun-Chen Liao, Akhilesh Kr. Singh, Uddipta Kar, Wei-Li Lee, Guang-Yu Guo
abstract: We investigate the superconducting properties of RuO$_2$ films grown on TiO$_2$ substrates by combining film fabrication and transport measurement with \textit{ab initio} calculation. Experimentally, we grow several RuO$_2$ (110) thin films on TiO$_2$ (110) substrates and observe superconductivity with critical temperature ($T_c$) of $\sim$2.0 K in 20-nm and 30-nm RuO$_2$ (110) thin films. Theoretically, we study the superconductivity in both RuO$_2$ (110) and RuO$_2$ (100) epitaxial films within McMillan formalism of isotropic Migdal-Eliashberg theory. Among the salient results, the calculated phonon dispersion relations of all the considered RuO$_2$ films show that the epitaxial films are dynamically stable. Importantly, our \textit{ab initio} calculations reveal that independent of the film orientation, the [001] compressive strain $ε_{[001]}$ pushes the flat Ru $d_{z^2}$-dominant bands towards the Fermi level ($E_F$), and significantly soften the out-of-plane acoustic phonon mode near the R point in the Brillouin zone, which substantially enhances the electron-phonon coupling (EPC) strength $λ$ and hence the calculated $T_c$ in the RuO$_2$ films. Remarkably, the amount of the phonon softening and the enhanced $T_c$ increase almost linearly with the increasing $ε_{[001]}$. The calculated $T_c$ for the films with thickness of $\geq$ 20 nm agree well with the experimental $T_c$. These findings demonstrate that among other things, lattice mismatch strain provides an effective route for tuning phonon-mediated superconductivity in RuO$_2$ and other thin films.
summary: This work demonstrates that lattice mismatch strain is a powerful tool for tuning superconductivity in $	ext{RuO}_2$ thin films. By combining experiments and theory, the authors show that compressive strain enhances the electron-phonon coupling ($\lambda$) through phonon softening. This mechanism provides a clear, tunable pathway for engineering superconducting materials.
main_problem: The study investigates how lattice mismatch strain can enhance phonon-mediated superconductivity in $	ext{RuO}_2$ thin films.
main_result: Compressive strain significantly enhances the electron-phonon coupling ($\lambda$) by softening low-energy phonon modes, leading to a calculated $T_c$ that agrees well with experimental observations.
method: The research combines experimental transport measurements with advanced *ab initio* calculations using the McMillan-Allen-Dynes formalism.
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{RuO}_2$ thin films grown epitaxially on $	ext{TiO}_2$ substrates, studied for both (110) and (100) orientations.
key_observables: Superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$), electron-phonon coupling strength ($\lambda$), and phonon dispersion relations.
important_parameters: Compressive strain ($\epsilon_{[001]}$), film thickness ($t$), and the Fermi level ($E_F$).
main_assumptions: The theoretical analysis uses the strained-bulk approach for thicker films and relies on the McMillan formalism for superconductivity.
figures_summary: Figures show XRD scans confirming film growth, resistivity vs. temperature curves showing superconductivity, and theoretical plots detailing phonon dispersions, DOS, and the enhancement of $\lambda$ with strain.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from experimental observation of superconductivity in $	ext{RuO}_2$ films to theoretical modeling, demonstrating how strain modifies the electronic structure (DOS) and vibrational properties (phonon softening), ultimately predicting enhanced $T_c$.
why_interesting: While focused on superconductivity, the mechanism relies heavily on coupling between electronic states and lattice vibrations (phonons), which is a core concept in many-body physics relevant to open quantum systems and material characterization.
